record.original_question: For the higher-order Toeplitz-determinant polynomials P_n^r(z) built from a finite sequence {f_k}_{k=0}^n, if the polynomial sum_{k=0}^n f_k z^k has only real negative zeros, must P_n^r(z) also have only real negative zeros for every r >= 2?

evidence.quote: A similar conjecture can be also be stated for polynomials formed by higher order Toeplitz determinants, namely, P_n^r(z) := ... It is probably not too hard to prove that the polynomial P_n^r(z) has degree n - r(r - 1).
Conjecture 2. Suppose the polynomial sum_{k=0}^n fk z^k has only real negative zeros. Then the same holds for the polynomial P_n^r(z) for each r >= 2.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $n \ge 1$ be an integer and let $f(z) = \sum_{k=0}^{n} f_k z^k$ be a polynomial of degree $n$ with real coefficients. For each integer $r \ge 1$, define the higher-order Toeplitz-determinant polynomial of order $r$ associated with $f$ by
$$
P_n^{\,r}(z) \;:=\; \sum_{\substack{k_1+k_2+\cdots+k_r = n\\ k_i \ge 0}} \binom{n}{k_1,k_2,\ldots,k_r}\, f_{k_1}f_{k_2}\cdots f_{k_r}\, \det\!\Bigl[\,(z+j-i)_{k_i}\,\Bigr]_{i,j=1}^{r},
$$
where $(a)_m := a(a+1)(a+2)\cdots(a+m-1)$ (with $(a)_0 := 1$) denotes the Pochhammer symbol and $\binom{n}{k_1,\ldots,k_r}$ is the multinomial coefficient. One can show that $P_n^{\,r}(z)$ is a polynomial in $z$ of degree $n - r(r-1)$.

Question. Suppose that the polynomial $f(z) = \sum_{k=0}^{n} f_k z^k$ has only real negative zeros. Must it then be the case that, for every integer $r \ge 2$, the polynomial $P_n^{\,r}(z)$ also has only real negative zeros?
artifact.category_tag: Zeros of polynomials and Toeplitz determinants
artifact.status_search_result: The conjecture appears in a December 2023 collection of open problems on polynomial zero distributions arising from the 2023 "Hausdorff Geometry of Polynomials" workshop, and is stated there as an unresolved conjecture extending a known second-order case. No subsequent paper claiming a proof or counterexample was found.

status_evidence.title: Open problems on polynomials, their zero distribution and related questions: 2023
status_evidence.snippet: Collects open problems presented at the 'Hausdorff Geometry of Polynomials' workshop (Sofia, July 2023).
status_evidence.claim: The conjecture about higher-order Toeplitz determinant polynomials P_n^r(z) is posed as an open problem in this 2023 compilation.

status_evidence.title: Totally nonnegative matrices, chain enumeration and zeros of polynomials
status_evidence.snippet: Recent work on zero-preserving operations and totally nonnegative matrices does not address this specific Toeplitz-determinant conjecture.
status_evidence.claim: No resolution of the higher-order Toeplitz-determinant conjecture appears in recent literature on real-rootedness.
